s: Contains an excellent collection of art from Cambodia's "golden age" of Angkor, and a lovely courtyard at the centre. A main attraction is the statue of King Jayavarman VII (1181-1219) in a meditative pose. Other exhibits worth seeing include graceful statues of Hindu gods, ancient stelae (tablets) inscribed in…
places.ad: St 13, Sangkat Chey Chumneas, Khan Daun Penh

places.n: The Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda
places.pu: entry, as Wikivoyage gives it
s: The King of Cambodia still lives here, but much of the palace is open to the public. The manicured gardens are nearly as dazzling as the colorful glass tiles of the palace roof. The two magnificent pagodas in the Palace Grounds, the Silver Pagoda and the Temple of the Emerald Buddha, are among the few public…

Phnom Penh is a bite-sized town, and it's easy to combine sightseeing, shopping, eating and drinking into a single walk through the city. The key to connecting the dots is the town's riverside promenade, Sisowath Quay, which runs along the west bank of the Tonle Sap River. Every morning, the Quay kicks off with a…
places.img: Sangkat Chey Chumneah, Phnom Penh 12206, Cambodia - panoramio (15).jpg

places.n: The Killing Fields of Choeung Ek
places.pu: entry, as Wikivoyage gives it
places.pt: US$6, including audio tour (not sold separately)
s: This is where the Khmer Rouge killed many thousands of their victims during their four-year reign of terror. Today the site is marked by a Buddhist stupa packed full of over 8,000 human skulls. The sides are made of glass so the visitors can see them up close. There are also pits in the area where mass graves were…
places.img: Buddhist Stupa at Choeung Ek killing fields, Cambodia.JPG

s: Impressive Buddhist-style Independence Memorial, commemorating the departure of the French in 1953, dominates the centre of the city. Nearby is the Stalinist-style Liberation Memorial, marking the Vietnamese capture of the city in 1979. The area is especially popular on weekend nights with locals when…

places.pu: entry, as Wikivoyage gives it
places.pt: 6,000 riel to get in, 500 riel to check your things
s: Built in the 1960s for the Asian Games that never happened, this interesting complex in the Modern-style has been sold off to the Taiwanese, in a murky deal by the Cambodian government. The new owners have renovated it and it has begun to be used once again as a venue. However in the evenings a walk around the top…

Historically, the wat was favoured by royalty. In the 1930s, it housed a charming young novice named Saloth Sar, who "never caused anyone any trouble, never started fights - a lovely child". Later in life, he changed his name to Pol Pot.

places.pu: entry, as Wikivoyage gives it
s: This hilltop pagoda marks the spot where the city was founded, and is always busy with pilgrims and fortune-tellers. The temple is notable more for its historic importance than physical structure, but the park is a pleasant green space and a popular gathering place for locals, and the murals inside the temple are…
Dates back to 1422 and is one of the five original founding monasteries of Phnom Penh.
Offers free meditation session on Mondays and Thursdays at 18:00.

places.pu: entry, as Wikivoyage gives it
places.pt: Adult 20,000 riel, 32,000 riel with audioguide; child 2,000 riel, 14,000 riel with audioguide
s: Opened 2019, this is a modern museum about money. 2,000 years of Cambodia’s monetary history through display cases and panels enhanced by multimedia presentations, and interactive exhibits. Even if you are not generally interested in economics, the museum tells the story of the Cambodian economy in an engrossing…

places.n: Phnom Tamao Zoological Park and Wildlife Rescue Center (PTWRC)
s: This is the largest zoo in Cambodia, and it's unique because it's made up of animals that have been rescued from illegal wildlife trade, sometimes for the final purpose of ending up on the dining room table. Among the residents are a number of sun bears and tigers. A full-scale tour is rather pricey at ~US$120, but…
places.ad: National Road No 2, Tro Pang Sap Village, Tro Pang Sap Commune, Ba Ti District

places.pu: entry, as Wikivoyage gives it
s: Boats leave every evening for a river cruise. Many provide snacks or dinners at sunset. Be sure to visit Mekong Island to see rural life.

A German-Cambodian cultural center that's an outgrowth of Germany's Goethe Institute. Art gallery, bar, mini-cinema and production house. Shows free, high quality foreign and Cambodian films Tu-Su nights at 19:00 in the bar-lounge in the front yard.
The only casino in Phnom Penh.

places.pu: entry, as Wikivoyage gives it
places.pt: Pistol US$20; AK-47 (30 rounds) US$40; rocket launcher US$350
s: Shooting range run by a unit of the Royal Cambodian Army. For a pretty hefty fee you can fire everything from pistols to machine guns at paper targets. Moto drivers, apparently oblivious of the reaction most visitors have, will try to include this in a trip to the killing fields and will take a nice commission for…

A touristy and pricey market with a beautiful 1930s Art Deco covered market near the Riverfront (Sisowath Quay) district. Its architecture is worth admiring. The market is well laid out, and sells everything from flowers to electronics to food. Some stalls inside the market are owned by ethnic Chinese, so if you…

This is a proper and authentic Cambodian market with inexpensive produces and everything regular Cambodians need on a day to day basis. No fine art decor can be found here, and some tourists may be put off by its rawness. However, many small eateries can be found around the market, some even inside the market,…

places.pu: entry, as Wikivoyage gives it
s: Good for local food with many food stalls. Sells clothes as well but you need to haggle. Usually some live entertainment, but is primarily for the locals. Friendly neighborhood atmosphere; eat barefoot sitting on mats on the ground.
places.img: Kabobs at Phnom Penh Night Market.jpg

s: Olympic Market was built in 1994 and is a local favorite with shoppers looking for wholesale fabrics, everyday wear, religious paraphernalia and traditional Khmer dresses. Buyers can look forward to big discounts in this market especially if they are buying in bulk. The market is well laid out and is one of the…

Renovated, renamed and made more upmarket in 2018. It is air-conditioned and contains a range of fast food outlets including Starbucks, Asian Kitchen, Bonchon as well as the well-stocked Lucky Supermarket and Guardian pharmacy all on the ground floor. There is a multi-screen Major cinema on the 5th floor. On the…

Phnom Penh's first of three giant Aeon Mall's, located in central city (opened mid-2014) with many brand name and Japanese stores. It has a supermarket, many restaurants and 7 screen, including one 4DX, Major Cineplex Cinema on 2nd floor. Newer Mall 2 (north of city) and Mall 3 (south of city) are much bigger.

Phnom Penh's second Aeon Mall and double the size of Aeon Mall 1, located north of city (opened May-2018) with many brand name and Japanese stores. It has a supermarket, many restaurants and multi screen, Major Cineplex Cinema, including an IMAX.

Phnom Penh's third and biggest of three huge Aeon Mall's, located south of city (opened Dec-2022) with many brand name and Japanese stores. It has a supermarket, many restaurants and multi screen, Major Cineplex Cinema. Airport Express Bus stops here midway to airport, at stop AEB 7, download free City Bus app to…
A multi-purpose development with upmarket shops and restaurants including a Starbucks, Hard Rock Cafe and Legend cinema on the 2nd floor, above Hard Rock Cafe.
There are three Thai Huot supermarkets in Phnom Penh.

places.pu: as Wikivoyage gives it
s: This lady serves inexpensive and super delicious local curries with noodles and an immense portion of meat at an unbeatable price. The only catch is that you either take-away or seat yourself onto one of the tiny chairs around her place, but without any table to put your bowl. However, the dish is definitely worth…

places.pu: as Wikivoyage gives it
s: Vegetarian restaurant with a variety of dishes including Chinese and Western options. Order by writing the item numbers on a laminated sheet with the marker provided.
places.ad: 15 Samdach Preah Thoamak Lekhet Ouk St

s: Small, traditional Indonesian restaurant in a tourist area.
Comfortable, nicely decorated corner restaurant with free Wi-Fi and some good dishes from a varied menu, including SE Asian. Their club sandwich is excellent. Perhaps a little over-priced.

About the only thing Aussie about this place is the owner. Foster's has, in keeping with Aussie trends, been banished from the place. But the food is very good and the wood-fired oven pizza matches anything found in Italy.

places.n: Java Creative Cafe Toul Tom Poung
s: Soups, salads and sandwiches in a cosy setting overlooking the Independence Monument. Good vegetarian options. Has a rotating art exhibition.

The BBK1 area is experiencing great growth in construction and becoming continually more an upmarket area of the city. At the junction of St 51 and St 310, each corner now has a multinational joint, KFC, Burger King, Carl's Jnr (California flame grilled burgers) and Gloria Jean's coffee.

places.pu: as Wikivoyage gives it
s: Delicious Nepali and Indian food for reasonable prices in a restaurant setting with free water and condiments.
Very popular with expats who hang out here. Owner Sony and his family are very friendly and helpful.
Popular place with a good selection of sandwiches, quiches, salads and freshly baked goods plus nice coffee too. Has a cosy and quiet courtyard seating area. Very good breakfast options.

places.pt: Prices shown on menu in US dollars.
s: American Restaurant that mainly serves Western dishes and a limited selection of Khmer dishes. Large selection of imported soft drinks and alcohol available. Popular with expats, staff are friendly and speak English.
places.hrs: Tue-Thu Sun 07:00-21:00, Fri Sat 07:00-22:00, Mon closed

s: French wine and cocktails bar with gourmet food. Famous for its near half price US$3 martinis on Saturday nights 21:00-00:00.

In the evenings at Sun & Moon Urban Hotel, guests and local residents can chill out in style at Cloud 9, the hotel’s rooftop bar, with cool beats, creative cocktails, and spectacular views over Phnom Penh city. Poolside BBQ parties and buffet dinners can also be arranged at this location.

places.pu: entry, as Wikivoyage gives it
s: Tallest sky bar in Phnom Penh, is a hidden gem in the heart of the city’s business district. From the roof of the 22-story Hyundai Phnom Penh Tower, the view of the city is breath-taking, and the soft mix of pop music in the background adds to the bar’s relaxed ambiance.

Polished concrete, gun-metal grey floor, chocolate leather seats and fabulously backlit bar serving some of the best and most inventive cocktails in town. One of the only slate pool tables in town. As much a mid-week bar as a weekend bar.

per night, as Wikivoyage gives it
per night, as Wikivoyage gives it
s: One of the cleanest and most conveniently located guesthouses you can find. TV, Wi-Fi, laundry, bus and flight tickets. French, English and Chinese spoken. Often the cheaper rooms are full.

places.pu: per night, as Wikivoyage gives it
s: A very laid back small guesthouse on the 2nd and 3rd floor with a cosy, sociable atmosphere and friendly staff. The cheaper rooms are very noisy. Surprisingly good food.

places.pu: per night, as Wikivoyage gives it
s: Nice backpackers guesthouse with friendly and helpful English and Norwegian management. Dorm beds & private rooms. A large stylish bar. Great for meeting other backpackers, with regular events and live music. Free Wi-Fi.

places.pu: per night, as Wikivoyage gives it
s: English and French spoken. Breakfast. Western and Asian restaurant, free Wi-Fi. Easy reservation and secure payment on-line. 100 rooms. Clean and stylish Khmer furnishings. Air-con, desk, tiled/marble floors, cable TV, minibar, private safes, elevator, safe at reception, bar and terrace, non-smoking floor, tour…

places.n: The Lone Star Saloon Bar and Guesthouse
places.pu: per night, as Wikivoyage gives it
s: Texas-themed restaurant with 3 apt-sized rooms upstairs available as guesthouse rooms. On a quiet street near the riverside. Air-con, hot water, free fast Wi-Fi, mini fridge stocked with drinks at bar prices. Caters to local expats and provides travel info for those new to Cambodia. Quiz nights on Monday 19:30.…

places.pu: per night, as Wikivoyage gives it
s: 19 spacious and stylish rooms with wifi & free breakfast. Overflow 13 x 5 m swimming pool surrounded by a leafy tropical garden, garden restaurant and bar. All rooms are equipped with air-con/fan, 22 inch LCD TV with international channels, DVD player.

places.pu: per night, as Wikivoyage gives it
s: 14 bright and spacious rooms with air conditioning and TV.

places.pu: per night, as Wikivoyage gives it
s: A hotel and apartment complex in two buildings separated by a yard with large trees and a small swimming pool. Wi-Fi, Air-con and several lounges. Breakfast available.

places.pu: per night, as Wikivoyage gives it
s: A copy of an Australian country club, financed by a rich Chinese owner. There is an open-air kids' swimming pool (covered with a net to avoid too much sun), an outdoor swimming pool where the expats send their kids to learn to swim. Surrounded by nice lounge chairs for sunbathing and relaxing. Horseback riding,…
places.ad: St 2004 Group 6 Toeuk Thla, District Russey Keao

places.pu: per night, as Wikivoyage gives it
s: On one of central Phnom Penh’s busiest commercial streets. The elegant white concrete façade typical of the Sankum era’s urban heritage has been restored to its former splendor. Ten apartments (60-120 m²) have been designed and decorated, each in a unique interpretation around the themes of luxury and travel. Has a…
places.ad: 123 St 110, corner St 19, Sangkat Wat Phnom

places.pu: per night, as Wikivoyage gives it
s: Phnom Penh's grand old hotel, built in 1929 by the French, used as a dry fish store by the Khmer Rouge, but given a thorough redecoration by the Raffles Group in 1999. Walking distance to Wat Phnom and the river, excellent service, wonderful attention to detail and the "Landmark" rooms in the old wing still use…

places.pu: per night, as Wikivoyage gives it

s: Hotel in a French colonial style building. The attached bistro The Shop is delicious and opens at 06:30, making it a solid choice for an early breakfast even if you're not staying at the hotel.

places.pu: entry, as Wikivoyage gives it
places.pt: US$12; audio guide in many languages US$5 (credit card accepted)
s: A modern museum with exhibits covering the history of the Khmer Empire, and the art, architecture, clothing, and culture of Khmer civilization, with a special focus on the Angkor complex. It is worth spending a couple of hours in the air-conditioned galleries as a break from visiting temples. Lots of pre-Angkorian…

places.pu: entry, as Wikivoyage gives it
s: A demining organization that uses trained rats to sniff out land mines, a strategy which is much faster and safer than using metal detectors (if the rats step on a mine, they are too light to set it off). The visitor's center has guided tours including examples of land mines and UXO (unexploded ordnance) and a…
places.ad: Trapeang Ses Village, Kouk Chauk Commune, Koumai Road
places.hrs: Daily tours every half hour 08:30–11:30 and 13:00–16:30

places.pu: entry, as Wikivoyage gives it
s: Beautifully kept gardens and mini zoo and playground with Rukha Cafe & Restaurant and a kids' library. A great place to visit just after visiting Apopo.

places.pu: entry, as Wikivoyage gives it
places.pt: Adult US$5, free for kids less than 12
s: The lotus silk farm offers guided tours every hour, providing visitors with a comprehensive understanding of the lotus silk production process. For those seeking a more hands-on experience, the farm also offers handicraft workshops where participants can learn Cambodian traditional handicraft techniques. The farm…

places.pu: entry, as Wikivoyage gives it
s: An 85-m-high Ferris wheel with 48 four-person baskets able to accommodate up to 192 people. The trip takes 18 minutes. It is the third highest Ferris wheel in Asia.

A large colony of day time flying fruit bats (they can see unlike most smaller species of bat), can be found hanging around in some of the tall trees in the parkland adjacent to the Royal Residence, an amazing sight you don't expect to see in the center of town.

As one of the oldest temples it makes a nice contrast between the oldest and the glittering new ones, though the rough artwork wouldn't match the craftsmen of Angkor. The architecture of the ramshackle open air hall next to the main building blends French-style arches and balustrades with Thai-influenced Buddhist…
places.ad: Samdech Tep Vong St and St 22

s: A landscaped temple with many stupas, a small decorative pool, and a school on the premises. Within the site of the temple is the Center for Khmer Studies, an open reading library with materials about the art, culture and history of Southeast Asia with specific interests in Cambodia.

The glittering modern temple grounds give few hints as to its 500-year history. Though the lotus-themed architecture seems to emulate temples from over the border, the front gate integrates Bayon-style heads and a scene in relief of the Buddha seated under a tree, while armies fire arrows on one side and others are…

places.n: Wat Thmei Temple & Stupa Memorial to the Killing Fields
places.pu: entry, as Wikivoyage gives it
s: A large Buddhist temple. In the grounds is a stupa with glass sides contains bones and skulls of victims of Pol Pot's army. Be wary of people purporting to be guides or asking for donations. Also, several of the photographs on the display boards are actually of the Holocaust in Nazi Germany. Take this attraction…

places.pu: entry, as Wikivoyage gives it
s: Showcases Cambodia’s rich cultural heritage, traditional performing arts. Dancers, singers and musicians.

places.pu: entry, as Wikivoyage gives it
s: Phare performers use theater, music, dance, comedy and modern circus arts, to tell uniquely Cambodian stories; historical, folk and modern. It's typically a 15-minute tuk tuk ride from Siem Reap town centre ($3).

places.pu: entry, as Wikivoyage gives it
s: Banteay Srey Butterfly Centre is a community development project and tourist destination just down the road from the Landmine Museum and Banteay Srey temple. Revenue from admissions is used to pay families in remote villages who are farming butterflies for the exhibit. The project makes a real difference to the…

places.pu: entry, as Wikivoyage gives it
places.pt: US$10 adult, US$7 child, US$4 Khmer adult, US$2 Khmer child
s: A park with butterflies amongst many species of plants and flowers, with waterfalls and ponds.

places.pu: entry, as Wikivoyage gives it
s: This mangrove forest offers a much more authentic floating village experience than the one close to the Tonlé Sap ferry harbour. This fascinating fishing village on stilts can be reached by tuk-tuk, motorcycle, or taxi from Siem Reap. It takes about 1 hour to reach the village, depending weather conditions. Beware…

places.pu: entry, as Wikivoyage gives it
s: This tiny museum was set up by local deminer Aki Ra to educate locals and tourists about the dangers of land mines. Piles of defused mines and unexploded ordnance (UXO) lie around the site and the guides are mostly teenagers who were orphaned or injured by mines, many of whom live on-site. This is a very worthwhile…

The highest hill in the area. Temple ruins similar to those found atop of Phnom Krom and Phnom Bakong can also be found on top of Phnom Bok. It lies 20 km to the north east of Siem Reap. Expect a tiring hike up the stairs. A guard may be able to show you around. Don't forget to check out the old howitzers from the…

The hill which dominates the view, as you approach the floating village of Chong Kneas from Siem Reap. At the top, temple ruins similar to the other two hills can be found. This particular hill is popular for sunsets, as it can be viewed over the flooded plains during the wet season, and over incredibly vibrant…

places.pu: entry, as Wikivoyage gives it
s: Collection of old (mainly Russian) tanks, artillery, landmines, handguns etc. Also some history background about the Cambodian civil war is displayed. Worthwhile for a 1-2 hour visit if interested in military.
places.img: Cambodian Civil War-era T-54 or Type 59.jpg

places.pu: entry, as Wikivoyage gives it
s: Daily pottery classes for beginners as well as professionals in pottery making, carving and glazing by local potter, Mrs Paruth Hann. Make your own design and take your glazed pot home as a souvenir. An enjoyable experience whilst supporting an enterprise creating fair wage jobs for the poor village women in Siem Reap.

places.pu: entry, as Wikivoyage gives it
s: Daily handicraft classes for kids and adults in yarn spinning, paper, incense stick-making and bracelet-making taught by local experts.

places.pu: entry, as Wikivoyage gives it
s: With the pottery class and clay class course, you can make your own ceramic artifact on the potter wheel. After you finish your piece, you can add different designs on it with potter's tools. With the painting activities, you can draw and / or paint your own design on a pot, cup, plate or other kinds of ceramics…
This is a fun, safe, creative, indoor-outdoor play and activity and education center with day care service and restaurant, for kids up to 8 years old.

places.pu: entry, as Wikivoyage gives it
s: This is possibly the nicest and biggest outdoors playground in Siem Reap. It's under a circular canopy and is in good condition. There are clean bathroom facilities for kids and a mini cafe and shop nearby. There are also basketball courts behind for older kids.
Play with the cats and a dog in this cat adventure playground cafe.

places.pu: entry, as Wikivoyage gives it
places.pt: US$68-790 per person depending on the tour
s: Private guided tours of the Angkor temples and the Siem Reap countryside by pedal-assist electric mountain bike, vintage Jeep or Vespa. Women-owned company founded in 2013. Licensed guides, and hotel pickup is included. The evening street food tour also runs as a small group.

places.pu: entry, as Wikivoyage gives it
s: Excellent wakeboarding park and only one in Cambodia.

places.n: KKO - Off Track Mountain Bike Tours
places.pu: entry, as Wikivoyage gives it
s: KKO is a local charitable non-profit NGO. They offer unique Angkor park and countryside off track bike tours. The entire profit generated from the bike tours flows back to the local KKO School. US$35 for a guided hlaf day bike tour and US$45-60 for a full day bike tour. Booking is required.

Explore the Cambodian countryside on a guided motorbike adventure or in a Jeep. On tour, get off the beaten path to discover authentic, rugged, and fascinating Cambodia. Sabai Moto and Jeep Adventures tours start from Siem Reap.

places.pu: entry, as Wikivoyage gives it
s: Cambodian cooking classes in a village 10 min from town. The classes are three hours long and include a visit to a local family and information on Cambodian cooking customs and beliefs. Hands on classes for a maximum of six people unless you book a private group.

places.pu: entry, as Wikivoyage gives it
s: This Thai fad has crossed the border. Dip your feet in a tank of fish and wince as they eat the dead skin off your toes. Trying a tank with feet already inside it will tell you if the fish are hungry. Some claim to have no piranhas while others offer a free beer to subdue any doubts.

places.pu: entry, as Wikivoyage gives it
s: Wonderful spa with a nice atmosphere, peaceful rooms, and experienced staff. The massages actually feel like trained people are giving them. No special services or hidden fees. It is a nice place to go as a couple or alone. They have massage tables and air conditioning. Tasteful exterior surrounded by frangipani…

places.pu: entry, as Wikivoyage gives it
s: Lovely little spa with a relaxing atmosphere and experienced staff. 60 minute Khmer massages are US$16, while 90 minute Khmer massages are US$23. They also offer oil massages, "spiritual massages," and manicures/pedicures. Treatment rooms have air conditioning, and they provide a cool drink before treatment and…

places.pu: entry, as Wikivoyage gives it
s: Family-run massage spa offering traditional Khmer massage, Swedish massage, aromatherapy, deep tissue, foot massage, four-hand massage and body care treatments. Treatments can be chosen on arrival.
Eclectic collection of clothes and trinkets. Bargain. Most stalls carry the same selection so you can shop around and find the cheapest price.
Inexpensive fruits, meat, snacks and half a dozen local eateries with noodle and curry dishes for 3–4,000 riel.
2 floors. Serves a variety of Italian and other European food with Britney Spears music videos in the background.

places.pu: as Wikivoyage gives it
s: A bright orange Mexican restaurant. Burritos, enchiladas, and quesadillas are reasonably authentic considering the location. They have some Khmer dishes if you want to eat more local food while enjoying the view over the balcony.

places.pu: as Wikivoyage gives it
s: Classic British-style fish and chips with mushy peas or coleslaw, and bread and butter.

places.pu: as Wikivoyage gives it
s: Serving Western dishes; chicken tenders, grilled cheese, crispy chicken apple salad, German chocolate cake, seasonal muffins, cinnamon rolls and some Asian dishes. All profit goes to fund local humanitarian projects through NGO People for Care & Learning. Air-con & high speed Internet.

places.pu: as Wikivoyage gives it
s: Tasty Cambodian food with lots of vegetarian options. Try the white mint tea shake.
places.img: Spring rolls at Bong Srey Mith Laor.jpg

places.pu: as Wikivoyage gives it
s: Absolutely phenomenal Khmer food. The other dishes are great as well. Always full, with locals, tourists and expats alike. But they'll magically make a seat for you, somehow.
places.hrs: Daily 07:00-21:00. Sometimes closes a bit early

places.pu: as Wikivoyage gives it
s: Delicious western-style cafe dishes, many healthy options and good Italian-style coffee.

places.pu: as Wikivoyage gives it
s: A popular restaurant with a good selection of both Khmer and Western food.
Comfortable air conditioned cafe that trains young people in hospitality and supports local community education projects. It also runs Khmer language classes. Board games and books available.
This is a locally owned cafe, the owner is Australian trained. The staff are mostly people with mild disabilities, their menus are labelled for vegan and gluten-free options.

places.pu: as Wikivoyage gives it
s: Sit outside in a big, soft, minimalist chair in the shade of a tree while you eat delicious vegetarian versions of Cambodian and international dishes. s: Stylish Khmer restaurant that is often so full you will have to wait for a table. The extensive menu is a mix of Khmer and Asian-esque dishes and with some vegetarian options. Some say the food is not spicy enough but the outdoor setting is nice if it is not raining.
Training restaurant teaching disadvantaged young adults. Cambodian, Asian, Western Food, with many vegetarian/vegan options.

places.pu: as Wikivoyage gives it
s: Cosy restaurant offering Organic Khmer and Western food of high quality. The vegetables are from the uncle´s farm, which can also be visited on a nice and educating half-day tour. Plenty of vegetarian and even vegan options available. They also offer cooking classes for Khmer cooking. The dishes are rich and…
Burger joint. Eat in or takeaway.

places.pu: as Wikivoyage gives it
s: Delicious Khmer and international food.

places.pu: as Wikivoyage gives it
s: French food. Exquisite cuisine made by a passionate chef, who prefers excellence and quality before all. Subtle and creative cuisine in a friendly atmosphere, bringing authentic French cuisine, wines and hospitality to Siem Reap.

places.pu: as Wikivoyage gives it
s: Local food along with good vegetarian options.

Probably Siem Reap's most daring restaurant, serving fusionesque Italian cuisine like foie gras on a bed of white asparagus and balsamic vinegar ice cream in a setting so achingly modern that the only decoration is a cloud of black dots on the white wall. A full meal with a glass or two of wine costs around US$100…

This restaurant is inside the colonial-era Raffles Hotel. Main courses include western and Khmer dishes, and range from US$20-30. Both the food and services were excellent. There are other restaurants in this hotel.

places.pu: as Wikivoyage gives it
s: French food with Cambodian influence. Only has two tasting menus, no à la carte dishes. Indoor and outdoor seating.

The quality of the food is excellent. Acclaimed by some as the best Khmer restaurant in all Cambodia, it is set in a chic hotel with a minimalist modern feel. The chefs source the freshest ingredients for both Khmer tasting menus, as well as a la carte dishes. Sit in air conditioned comfort, or outside tables and…

places.pu: entry, as Wikivoyage gives it
s: There is a strip of local Cambodian bars near the Platinum KTV. If you walk past it, there is a whole 2-3 block street full of local Cambodian bars. Menus are not in English and few employees speak English, but the prices are good. These are restaurant/bars, they have young women sitting at the entrance, and you…

It was the most famous backpacker bar in Siem Reap, directly across from competing late night spot Temple Club. US$1 draught beers, US$2 mixers, US$6-8 buckets. Large Western crowd. Offers inside and outside drinking. Open until late. As of October 2025 it looks like it has permanently closed..
Restaurant serving Khmer, Asian and Western food, with live music. Great cocktails. Opened in 2005 before Pub Street existed.

Open air rooftop bar featuring a 2-m skateboard halfpipe, jam sessions every Wednesday evening, live DJs and bands every week and a resident tattoo shop with a French artist. Probably the best city views in town, and unusual sunset over the halfpipe. At the end of Pub Street, look up for the X.
This sophisticated bar serves up delightful refreshing cocktails in a sultry red lounge plucked straight from 1930s Shanghai.

places.pu: per night, as Wikivoyage gives it

The hotel offers a range of bright, spacious and clean fan and air-con single, twin, double, and family rooms. The eerie charm of the abandoned French hill station that included a shell of a church and the isolated upland nature reserve are rapidly becoming a tacky resort. The road up the mountain is now paved and provides easy access. The cooler climate…

There are lots of durian farms on the way to Teuk Chhou Rapids. It may be hard to communicate to a tuk-tuk driver that this is what you want to see, but a tourist office / travel agent can help you arrange it. There don't seem to be organized guided tours like for the pepper farms, but you can go to a plantation…
Stand Up paddleboarding, SUP lessons and tours. Kayak rentals, swimming and cafe.
Mostly clothes, a bit of food and other miscellaneous products, and a couple of small rides for kids.

places.pu: as Wikivoyage gives it

Multi-storey purpose-built hotel.

Swanky garden bungalow resort.

Excellent rooftop restaurant and bar with a brilliant view overlooking…

An absolute must is to visit the Pepper plantation. The pepper used to be the number one pepper in the world and all the good French restaurants had it. It is having a revival with a local NGO (Farmlink) helping promote and plant it again.

A single, kilometre-long crescent of sand near the tip of the Kep peninsula. Tasty street food and fruit as well as beachwear is for sale along the road behind the beach. Busy on weekends, mainly with Cambodian visitors, but often deserted during the week. The road through Kep traces the coastline to the beach and…

s: There is an easy trail going full circle around the hill above Kep in the national park. It's a wonderful piece of jungle, in which it is quite probable to see some monkeys and other animals. The trail is about 8 km long (a 2-3 hour walk). If you don't want to walk, the path is big enough to ride a bicycle or a…
Rent catamarans, kayaks, and even a speedboat. They also have a restaurant with some special foods.
Crowded, noisy, humid outdoor market selling fresh seafood, plus drinks, dresses, and swimsuits for the tourists. Beachwear here is about half the price you'd pay at the shops by the beach.

The comfortable bar is replete with pool table and offers a good selection of Khmer and Western dishes including Swiss specialties cheese fondue and raclette. Music and liveliness can be enjoyed until midnight. Happy hour (17:30-19:00) lubricates the sun's decent over the infinity pool. Mojiot and draft beer available.

Its elevated position offers breeze and good views overlooking Kep and the ocean. The small menu offers burritos, pizzas and pancakes. There's a range of detailed maps of Kep and its surroundings. The helpful French owner has been living in Kep since 2004 and provides interesting company. Mountain bikes are…

Holy Crab is one of the nicest of the generally basic restaurants at the Crab Market. You can still find the seafood staples you should try in Kep, but everything is served in a nice ambiance. Wonderful for a leisurely dinner or enjoying a nightcap by the water.

A popular hang out for local expats, also a cosy place to enjoy an excellent sea side pizza and some great cocktails. They now boast an upstairs terrace overlooking the ocean. A truly stunning place for Kep's famous sunsets.

places.pu: per night, as Wikivoyage gives it

places.pu: per night, as Wikivoyage gives it

A popular infinity salt-water swimming pool, free bicycles, fast & free WiFi all…

places.pu: per night, as Wikivoyage gives it

places.pu: per night, as Wikivoyage gives it
s: Rustic, romantic bungalows amid the trees near Kep National Park. Helpful staff, wifi, several pet dogs and even a squirrel. Tasty, if a bit pricey, breakfast and dinner are available.

Amazing 4-km-long stretch of clean, white sands. Far less crowded and more relaxed than other beaches in Sihanoukville. Every season more and more beach bars and guesthouses pop up along the beach. Tourists will find accommodation in rooms or bungalows (prices ranging from US$5-30), e.g., Cinderella Beach…
Guesthouses, bars and restaurants right on the beach, open until the early hours. This beach is the most popular and typically has the greatest number of people on the beach.
Owned by Sokha Beach Resort. It is private, but you can access it by paying a couple dollars. You won't have many people begging or trying to sell you something here.

A waterfall approximately 7 km from the city of Sihanoukville and then a further 9 km along a red dust track. Popular swimming area, families come to spend the day, many food stalls, rest houses and other facilities line the stream. The swimming is the attraction more than the waterfall so don't expect much nature…
A restaurant serving local flavors and Cambodian traditions with an 8- or 12-course dinner option if you prefer.

places.pu: per night, as Wikivoyage gives it
s: Supposedly one of the last hostels in Sihanoukville. Features a small swimming pool and a bit overpriced Khmer food.

Spacious bungalows on a very quiet part of the beach. It has fan and air-conditioning rooms and a nice porch in front of the bungalow with comfortable chairs and couch and brilliant ocean view. Wi-Fi. There is also a nice little bar downstairs. No restaurant, but there are plenty nearby.

places.pu: per night, as Wikivoyage gives it
s: Hotel in a lush garden with a swimming pool, air-conditioning, hot showers, and free Wi-Fi, pick-up and shuttle to the beaches and city. It is a training hotel to help young Cambodians learn a skill and find a job.

An international-class beach resort. Very bland and a bit rough around the edges, but the beach is gorgeous and hassle-free, and the resort is family-friendly with children swimming pools and playgrounds. Try their best Restaurant, Lemongrass, and "The Deck" Tapas Bar. 180° views of the gulf.

places.pu: per night, as Wikivoyage gives it

A nice touch are some black and white photographs of the hotel in its heyday. The best feature is the adjacent clean pale sand private beach which has crystal clear water and…

places.pu: per night, as Wikivoyage gives it

Has wifi in the restaurant all day but limited electricity, and management will not let you use the power in the restaurant to charge devices during the daytime. Running water only available 08:00-10:00 and 18:00-20:00. Noticeably,…

places.pu: per night, as Wikivoyage gives it
s: In this calm resort, bungalows accommodate up to 5 people, tree-houses only 3. The tree houses however are as close to paradise as you can get, 10 m up the tree, well-furnished with a balcony overlooking the turquoise beach. Rooms have a plug, but power availability is shorter than in other resorts. Has great pizza.
Alone standing bungalows with private bathroom. Bungalows for US$20 and $30. Restaurant/Bar. Boat transfer from Sihanoukville and back US$20.
A small, friendly dive center run by professional experienced instructors, offering fun diving and SSI dive courses.
Travel agency in M'Pai Bay offering guided treks, boat tours, snorkeling tours, kayak rentals and guided kayak tours.
In the traditional fishing village of M'Pai Bay on north coast of Koh Rong Samloem. Beach bar and guesthouse, dorm rooms available. The soundtrack in the bar features funky tunes.
A nice beach front hotel with AC and hot water rooms, offering food and drinks options.
A nice resort in M'Pai Bay village featuring great views! Their restaurant is a great place to watch the sunset.

places.pu: per night, as Wikivoyage gives it

places.pu: entry, as Wikivoyage gives it
s: The shows are fun, energetic and exciting and include a range of circus disciplines. The ticket price helps support the NGO school which works with disadvantaged children and teenagers.
places.hrs: Probably the most interesting thing happening in Battambang. You can check their website for the schedule or find the ca

places.pu: entry, as Wikivoyage gives it
s: A hill with the killing caves of the Khmer Rouge, a few others caves adorned with Buddhist statues, and a monastery with two Buddhist stupas on the hilltop. The admission charge also includes Wat Banan. It takes about 1 hr to climb the circuit to the monastery on top, with a short-cut leading back down to the shops…
The so-called mini-Angkor Wat, an impressive flight of stairs lead up to a dilapidated Angkor-style temple which is still in use as a Buddhist shrine.

The most famous of these statues (Lok Ta Dambong Kra Nhoung) is on the main road from Phnom Penh and is of an ancient Khmer King holding a stick which he used to quell rebellions in the Battambang area. The name of the town and province derives from this legend.

Angkor-type temple ruin. The road runs along lovely small rivers flanked by trees and small villages making it a generally nice area. Approaching Wat Ek Phnom, you suddenly encounter a giant Buddha statue in the wat, which is certainly picture-worthy. The grounds of the wat also have an Angkorian-era temple which…

Roughly translates as "wat in the forest". An extremely old pagoda on the east side of the Sangker River. The eerie old wat was used as a Khmer Rouge prison, and there were many executions on the premises. A new pagoda is now being built, and there is a memorial to the victims of the Khmer Rouge regime, with…

places.pu: entry, as Wikivoyage gives it
s: Established in 1963, the Battambang Provincial Museum houses a small but impressive collection of Khmer artifacts. The core of the collection is statutes and temple pieces dating from the advent of Hindu and Buddhist religion in Cambodia all the way through the Angkor period. There is also a notable collection of…

places.pu: entry, as Wikivoyage gives it

s: The term "train" is here used loosely: a large bamboo platform mounted on train axles powered by a small go-kart engine. A trip on the train can be booked in most hotels or arranged with a motorbike/tuk-tuk driver. It is regulated by Battambang's Tourist Police, with a standard rate of US$5 per person, minimum 2…

Soksabike is a social enterprise dedicated to sustainable tourism in Battambang. They offer half day and full day bike tours around the countryside where guests can learn about the everyday life and culture of Cambodia. The money for the tour is distributed to families in the community along the way and goes to pay…

places.pu: as Wikivoyage gives it

Huge menu, and some great fruit shakes. This place is a bit more 'Asian' than Western, but is still full of foreigners. Service is chaotic, food is quite good, and the upstairs provides one of the few Battambang eateries where you get an outlook and a breeze.

places.n: Heng Chhay Ly Food Court (3rd Floor)

s: Home of Battambang's original cooking school, this restaurant remains highly popular. A nice range of Asian and Western dishes, US$3-4.50. Nice shakes. Host speaks fluent English and French. Central.
Open air ambience.
